name: How does a garage conversion compare to building a new home addition?
description: Garage conversions save time and structural costs by using the existing roof and slab, but you permanently trade away enclosed parking and storage.

mainEntity.name: How does a garage conversion compare to building a new home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Converting an existing garage is generally faster and requires less raw structural framing than building a detached accessory dwelling unit or ground-up home addition. By utilizing the existing foundation, exterior walls, and roof, you eliminate major excavation and foundation costs. The practical tradeoff is the permanent loss of covered vehicle parking and primary storage space. A standalone addition preserves your parking capacity and allows for greater architectural freedom in room dimensions, but it demands a larger yard footprint, broader permitting, and higher overall material and labor investment.
